title: feat(cloud-connection,metadata-protocol): an unmanaged copy can take the package's sample data, owned by the installer
body:
domain:server#3 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5pXkgNXVpCn2GZDjyy

Body: seat refresh (round 4) · 2026-11-08T08:16Z

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XJZfATGni9GCmv2TJRug9bZ)_

Fixes #30808

Clause-②: yes (widening) — the install-local door accepts an optional `seedSampleData` beside `installMode: 'unmanaged'`, and its answer may carry `copyRecord` when the door's record of the copy was not kept; the install-local purge door (`POST /marketplace/install-local/:id/purge-sample-data`) now reaches an unmanaged copy this door made, where it answered 404 for every id without a ledger entry; and the `importUnmanagedPackage` verb takes a door-stated `seedData`. The published `ImportUnmanagedPackageRequestSchema` is unchanged
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

1. 非托管安装新增可选开关 `seedSampleData`，默认关闭；关闭时行为与之前完全一致。
2. 打开后，示例数据以 `seed` 元数据项写入新的 base（即“种子回执”，存于环境元数据中），再由安装门以安装者身份一次性加载，`owner_id` 与 `created_by` 均为安装者；原包里不同角色拥有的行会合并为同一个拥有者。
3. 清除（purge）只对本安装门自己复制出的 base 生效（门在账本目录旁的 `unmanaged-copies/` 里私有记录每个副本，卸载时移除）；Studio 自建的 base 仍返回 404。记录绑定 base 实例：保存该 base 在 `sys_packages` 中那一行的 `version` 与 `created_at`，行不在或 `created_at` 不同（同 id 的后来 base）即返回 404。清除读取回执，按 `externalId` 精确删除复制的行，用户自建的行保留；base 已卸载时先答 404；记录读不到时返回 503 并指明要修复的本地文件；回执或包存储读不到时返回 503 请重试，均不删任何行。记录未能写入时，安装应答带 `copyRecord: { written: false, message }`。
   遗留条件两条：没有 `package` 服务的运行时没有 base 行，记录只按 id 匹配；同一秒内卸载并以同 id 重建的 base 共享 `created_at`。
   包存储的 `get` 遇到普通数据库错误（锁超时、连接断开）时记日志并返回 null，只有 seam 拒绝才抛出。因此普通错误在清除时答 404，在安装时则不写记录（`copyRecord` 会说明），两者都是失败即关闭；之后补写记录列为后续 #31425。
4. 重复安装仍返回 409；行间查找按加载顺序解析；`targetNamespace` 只改 `object` 名，记录与 `externalId` 原样保留。
5. 重启不会重新插入任何行（复制后、清除后都已用真实启动验证）；回执项单纯保存不加载任何行；发布时与任何环境 seed 项一样按 `externalId` 匹配、不重复加载；清除后再发布会按发布规则重新加载，这些行不带安装者为拥有者。
6. 无 spec 改动；前提更正：种子可携带文件字节（`files`，回执原样保留，副本上加载字节未经测试），框架本身没有记录配额；卸载前需先清除，否则行会留下；`seed` 列表读不出存储项的问题已立为 #31399。

## What changes

**The switch (`@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `POST /marketplace/install-local`).** `seedSampleData` is accepted beside `installMode: 'unmanaged'` and is off by default. Without it, an unmanaged copy loads no row and answers the same `seeded: { mode: 'skipped', … }` as before. With `true`, the door loads the copy's datasets once, inline, and answers `seeded: { mode: 'inline', inserted, updated, skipped, errors }`. A value that is not a boolean, or one sent with a managed install (which always loads its data), answers 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` before anything is written.

**Ownership.** Every copied row is owned by the person who installed it: the door loads with the installer as the load's user and stamps `owner_id` and `created_by` with that id (the #30324 option C / #30680 answer A rule). Rows the package wrote as different personas collapse to that one owner; the copy keeps no record of the persona a row had. So per-role answers in the customer's environment differ from the gallery's per-persona transcripts.

**The seed receipt (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `importUnmanagedPackage`).** Asked with the door-stated `seedData: true` (read off before the strict request parse, like `actor`), the verb writes each `data` dataset as a `seed` item of the new base, in the environment's own `sys_metadata`, after every other copied item: `<object>_seed`, then `<object>_seed_2` for a second dataset of the same object. This receipt is what the door loads from and what the purge deletes by. Under `targetNamespace` only the dataset's `object` follows the #30794 rename map; records and `externalId` are copied verbatim, because the rename's free-text rewrite would otherwise reach record values (a probe showed a record value `'crm_account'` rewritten to `'mycrm_account'`), and a changed key would break both lookups and the purge. A dataset that cannot be written (no `object`, no `records` array, a name past the storage limit) is refused with 400 before any write; a `seed` item the save door refuses rolls the whole copy back, as every copied item does; `seed` not runtime-creatable on the target is a finding on the key `data`. A re-run is still refused with 409.

Two receipt designs were weighed. A marker column on every seeded row would need a schema change on every object the package seeds, and a row the person later edits would still carry it. The receipt in the environment ledger needs no column, survives restarts with the base, and lets the purge run the same `externalId` match the managed purge already uses. The receipt was chosen.

**Reading the receipt.** Each receipt item is read through the protocol's by-name read (`getMetaItem`), scoped to the base. The list read cannot serve it: a `seed` body declares no `name` (`SeedSchema` is closed), and the list keys every stored item by its body's `name`, so `getMetaItems({ type: 'seed' })` serves no stored seed item at all (measured on the real showcase boot: 5 active rows in `sys_metadata`, 0 listed, each one served by name). On install the names come from the import's own answer (`copied`); on purge they come from the base's active `seed` rows in `sys_metadata`, read as the system for their names only. An item that is not served, or is not a dataset, fails the whole read.

**The door's record of its copies (`packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-unmanaged-copies.ts`).** Nothing a copy carries marks it as one: the base manifest holds only the source identity plus `id`, `name` and `namespace`; `<sourceId>-copy` is also the Studio duplicate's default id; and an unmanaged copy writes no ledger entry. So the door records each copy it makes, with or without sample data, as one JSON file per base under `unmanaged-copies/` in its storage directory, beside the install ledger. The ledger reads only the `.json` files at its own top level, so the record is never read as an install entry. Lifetime:
- It is written in the same act as the copy, before any row is loaded. A record that cannot be kept (its file cannot be written, or the package store does not answer with the new base's row) leaves the copy unreachable by the purge (404), never reachable by mistake. The install still answers 200 and says so in `copyRecord: { written: false, message }`, besides the log line; the answer carries no `copyRecord` when the record was kept, so that answer's key set is unchanged. No door records that copy later; re-recording is follow-up #31425.
- It is removed when the base is uninstalled, through a protocol uninstall cleanup (`install-local:unmanaged-copy-record`). That cleanup's outcome now appears in every uninstall answer's `cleanups`, `{ name: 'install-local:unmanaged-copy-record', success: true, removed: 0 }` for a package that is no recorded copy: the install-local `DELETE`, the protocol's `deletePackage`, and `DELETE /packages/:id` (`persisted.cleanups`, and the partial-failure 400). The shape of those answers is unchanged; the changeset says so.
- It is lost with the ledger directory, as ledger entries are.
- A copy made before this record existed has none, and the purge does not reach it.

**The record is tied to the base instance, not only to its id.** "This door once copied this id" can outlive the base: a protocol without the cleanup registry, a removal that failed, a base removed by another replica, or an uninstall racing the record write. A later base under the same id (a Studio duplicate also defaults to `<sourceId>-copy`) must not inherit the purge. So the record also keeps `instance`: the `version` and `created_at` of the base's row in the package store (`sys_packages`, read through the `package` service's `get`). The store mints `created_at` when it first inserts `(id, version)`, keeps it when the same base is published again (the publish is an upsert), and an uninstall deletes every row of the id, so a later base under the same id gets a row of its own. The purge reads the row of the recorded version again and answers 404 when it is gone or carries another `created_at`. No spec key was added. The base manifest's `hash` was not used, because it changes whenever the base is edited. Two conditions stay open, stated in the changeset and in the module docblock:
- a runtime with no `package` service persists no base row, so its record holds no `instance` and the purge's reach there is by id alone (such a base does not survive a restart either);
- `created_at` is the store's `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`, one-second resolution, so a base uninstalled and re-created under the same id within the same second shares it.

**A passing package-store error fails closed.** The package store's `get` (`service-package`) catches an ordinary driver error (a lock timeout, a dropped connection), logs it and answers `null`; it throws only its seam-unreadable refusal (a query seam that ran no read). The door cannot tell that `null` from a gone row. So at purge a passing store error answers 404 and deletes nothing, and at install it leaves the copy unrecorded, which `copyRecord` reports. Both fail closed. Only the seam refusal reaches the purge as a 503. The store is not changed here; re-recording an unrecorded copy is follow-up #31425.

**The purge (`POST /marketplace/install-local/:id/purge-sample-data`).** When the install ledger has no entry for the id, the purge first asks whether the base is still installed and writable (404 if not, before the record is read), then whether the door's record names it and its `instance` matches the package store's row (404 if not); every other id keeps the 404, a Studio-authored writable base with published `seed` items included. For a recorded copy made without the sample data it answers 400 `NOTHING_TO_PURGE`, saying no sample data was copied. Otherwise it reads the base's `seed` items and deletes exactly the rows they name by `externalId`; a row the person wrote in the same object survives. A record that cannot be read answers 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` naming the local record file to repair; a receipt that cannot be read, or a package store whose query seam ran no read, answers 503 asking for a retry, with no driver text in the answer. An ordinary package-store error answers 404, as above. Neither deletes anything: an unread receipt is never taken for "no sample data". The managed path is unchanged (the shared body moved into `purgeSeedDatasets`).

**No double load.** A boot never applies the receipt: a restart after the copy, or after the purge, inserts no row. A copied `seed` item saved later writes metadata only, even with every row of it gone. Drafted and published, it behaves as every environment `seed` item does: create-only, matched by `externalId`, so the rows already loaded are matched and none is inserted twice. Published after a purge, it loads its rows again under the publish rule, not the installer's: the publish names no person to the loader, so those rows carry no `owner_id` or `created_by`.

## Tests

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.test.ts`, describe "the sample data, copied when the door asks — the seed receipt (#30808)", 14 cases: off by default; planned after every other item, named `<object>_seed`, records verbatim; under `targetNamespace` only `object` renamed, records and `externalId` verbatim; `_seed_2` naming; a dataset missing `records` or `object` answers 400 with no writes; `seed` not runtime-creatable is a finding on `data`; the verb writes the seed rows into the new base with no `organization_id` and the response parses against `ImportUnmanagedPackageResponseSchema`; a refused `seed` item rolls back the whole copy with `failedItem: { type: 'seed', name: 'crm_lead_seed' }`; a re-run answers 409 with no writes; an undeclared key (`withSampleData`) answers 400; a dataset that carries `files` keeps the map in the receipt verbatim; a copied `seed` item saved with every row absent (the state after a purge) inserts nothing; drafted and published while its rows are there it inserts none (`matched: ['a1', 'a2']`, `inserted: 0`); drafted and published after a purge it inserts both rows with no `owner_id` or `created_by`.
- `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-install-modes.test.ts`, describe "install-local — an unmanaged copy's sample data, asked for with `seedSampleData` (#30808)", 17 cases, on the real `SeedLoaderService`: off by default; asked for, 3 rows inserted, `owner_id` and `created_by` the installer, a contact's `account` the id of the account it names, no ledger entry and no registry package; the purge deletes exactly 3 and keeps a user row, a second purge skips 3; a restart after the copy and after the purge inserts nothing; a re-run answers 409 with no new writes; a non-boolean value, or a managed install, answers 400; an unknown id answers 404 and an unreadable receipt answers 503 with no deletes; a Studio-authored writable base with published `seed` items is refused at purge with 404 and nothing deleted; a copy made before the record existed is refused with 404; the record sits beside the ledger, never listed as an install entry, keeps the base's `instance`, and an unreadable record answers 503 whose message names the record file and asks for no retry; a removed base with an unreadable record answers 404, not 503; a later base under the copy's id (same version, another `created_at`) is refused with 404 and nothing deleted, while the copy's seed items and rows are still there; at purge, an ordinary store error (which the store double, like the real store, answers `null`) answers 404, the store's seam refusal answers 503 naming no file and carrying no store text, a gone row answers 404, and the same row put back is reached again (3 deleted); with no `package` service the record holds no `instance` and the purge reaches the copy by id alone (the residual, pinned); a record that cannot be written, or a package store that meets an ordinary error or the seam refusal at install, is said in the install answer's `copyRecord` (no driver text) and the copy then answers 404 at purge, while a kept record adds no key; a copy made without the sample data answers that no sample data was copied; the uninstall cleanup removes the record, after which the purge answers 404.
- `packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-purge.test.ts`: `seedDatasetOfReceiptItem` keeps every member `SeedSchema` declares, `files` included, and answers `undefined` for anything that is not a dataset. `marketplace-install-local-uninstall-meta-reads.test.ts`: its `DELETE` answers now carry the copy-record cleanup's outcome (`removed: 0`).
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/install-local-unmanaged-seed-copy.dogfood.test.ts` (new), on the real showcase with one database file across three boots: the CRM example's copy answers 200 and loads its 28 rows inline; every row is owned by the signed-in installer; an activity's `account` resolves to the copied account it names; a restart inserts no row; the purge deletes exactly the 28 and keeps a row the person wrote; a restart after the purge inserts none back; the door's record keeps the base's `instance` (`version`, `created_at`) and the answer carries no `copyRecord`, and the purge in the second boot still reaches the copy, so a restart keeps the row's `created_at`.

## Acceptance notes

- **File bytes (premise correction).** A seed can carry file bytes: `SeedSchema` has a `files` map (`packages/spec/src/data/seed-file.zod.ts`), and the loader mints a `sys_file` per row from it. What is pinned: the receipt keeps a dataset's `files` verbatim, and the door's projection hands it to the loader. Loading those bytes on a copy is not exercised by a test here; it goes through the same loader a managed install uses.
- **Personas.** Rows owned by different personas in the package collapse to the installer, so per-role answers in the customer's environment differ from the gallery's per-persona transcripts.
- **Quotas.** The framework enforces no record quota on a seed load; the only quota-shaped setting found is `LifecycleService`'s in objectql, which a seed load does not read. Whether a cloud deployment enforces one on top is not verified here.
- **Uninstall.** Uninstalling the copy's base removes the receipt items and the door's record with it, and leaves the rows. Purge before uninstalling.
- **Residual of the instance tie.** On a runtime with no `package` service the record holds no `instance` and the purge reaches a copy by id alone; a base re-created under the same id within the same second shares `created_at`. Both are stated in the changeset and the module docblock; no spec key was invented.
- **Passing package-store errors.** An ordinary store error answers 404 at purge and leaves the copy unrecorded at install (`copyRecord` says so); both fail closed. Re-recording is follow-up #31425.
- **Counting and reseeding.** The listing's `withSampleData` count and the `reseed-sample-data` door read the install ledger, which an unmanaged copy never writes, so neither covers a copy yet.
- **Walled posture.** An unmanaged install is still refused under a walled posture; the door nonetheless loads in the caller's active organization when a wall is on, and answers `refused` without one.
- **Out of scope: the `seed` list, filed #31399.** `GET /meta/seed` (and `getMetaItems({ type: 'seed' })`) lists no stored `seed` item, whoever wrote it, because the list keys items by a body `name` that `SeedSchema` does not have. This PR works around it (reads by name) and does not change the list.
- **Out of scope.** The comment on `data: 'door'` in `packages/spec/src/kernel/unmanaged-install.ts` ("a copy of the metadata cannot carry them") is now stale. It is spec text, so it is left for the spec seat.

The purge pin has one row for each: ordinary error 404, seam refusal 503. The install pin also has one row for each, and both answer `copyRecord` with no record written. No production line changed this round, only docblocks and the changeset, so there is no new ablation.

  - the no-row failure at install → deleted: the unkept-record pin red.
